notes.1.86: 1.88-89: badly damaged; only isolated words can be read. 1.90, 1.96: s,t-qb,t, literally 'a cool thing', a refreshment or diversion. 1.99: bꜣw is taken as a boat; it may be a crew. 1.104-106: no change of speaker is written, though these lines read naturally as the king's reply. 1.105: sqb is an unidentified wood. 1.110: ḥt.n =s ('caught') is uncertain. 1.122: mostly restored; the sense is uncertain. 1.146: 'potsherd' is written on both sides of the gap. 1.172, 1.173, 1.235: the jp,wt of the sanctuary of Thoth are disputed: secret chambers, or their plans or count. 1.177: ḫnt[,j]-ẖty,t 'upstream' is uncertain. 1.178: ssnḏm is a dark wood. 1.180: sš 'threshold' is uncertain. 1.184: kḥkḥ,t-n.t-sry,t, taken as a wheezing cough, is uncertain; the syntax of the sentence is loose. 1.192: šnt ḫ,t 'contend in a matter' is uncertain. 1.193: ꜥfd.t ('hidden') is uncertain; 'He Who Clothes the Weary One' is a god's epithet. 1.229: ḫt-ꜥꜣ is an unidentified bird. 1.242: sjp.tj ('Inventory', 'Inspection') is the name of a room. 1.251: the sense is uncertain. 1.262: =s is probably for =sn ('of them'). 1.268-269, 1.271: ꜥꜣḏ.du 'the Two Fishes' (?) appears to be a waterway whose sandbanks are 'cut off', i.e. impassable; 'jw =s tj' and bꜣk ('labour') are uncertain. 1.283: Rꜥ-wsr is given as Rawoser. 1.295: obscure after the gap. 1.298, 1.310, 1.322: each name puns on Isis's words (wsr 'be strong', sꜣḥ 'kick', kkw 'darkness'); the three children are the Fifth Dynasty kings Userkaf, Sahure and Kakai, here written Userref, Sahra and Keku. 1.301, 1.313, 1.325: nḫb,t 'covering, inlay' is uncertain. 1.303: ḏb,t is the birth-brick. 1.339: obscure; tnmw may be a beer, nm.w is unknown. 1.379: obscure; zp-2 marks a repeated word. 1.388: šꜣj ('length') is uncertain. 1.402: damaged and obscure.
notes.1.66: Line 4: smwn taken as an affirming particle ('surely'). Line 13: šd,w mḥ,tj taken as 'the north field'. Line 15: qmꜣ.w is partly damaged; 'thrown' is the likely sense. Line 18: pꜣd, a pellet or ball of incense; šns, a kind of cake.
notes.1.49: Line 3: the damaged word jri̯ before jṯi̯.n is unclear and is left untranslated.
notes.1.1: Line 2: the lector priest's name is lost.
notes.1.8: ḥn,t is partly damaged and its sense here ('visit', 'journey') is uncertain; wn,t taken as 'sanctuary'.

nodes.text: [...] [Then] [the Majesty] of the Dual King Khufu, justified, [said]:

[Have] [1,000] [loaves of bread], 100 jugs of beer, [1] ox [and] [2] [pellets] [of incense] [presented] [to] the Dual King Djoser, justified, [and] [have] [1] [cake], [1] jug [of beer], a large joint of meat [and] [1] [pellet] [of incense] [given] [to] [the chief lector priest] [...],
[for] [I] have seen a token of his learning.
[It was] done according to [all] that [His] [Majesty] commanded.
Then the king's son Khafra stood up [to] [speak], [and] [he] [said]:
It was His Majesty who made the visit to [the sanctuary] [of] [Ptah], [and] the [chief lector] priest Webaoner [was] with [him].
Now when the commoner has gone down to the lake, as is his custom every day, you are to throw [the] [crocodile] [of] [wax] after him.
Then the [steward] threw the crocodile of wax into the water after him,
and it [became] a crocodile of 7 cubits.
Then it seized the commoner; [it] carried [him] off.
Then [he] gave [it] [to] [Webaoner].
[Then] [Webaoner] [took] it.
Then the Majesty of the Dual King Nebka, justified, said:
Surely this crocodile is fearsome!
Then Webaoner bowed down
and took hold of it,
and it was in his hand a crocodile of wax.
Then the chief lector priest Webaoner told again this matter that the commoner had done in his house with his wife to the Majesty of the Dual King Nebka, justified.
Then His Majesty said to the crocodile:
Take what is yours!
Then the crocodile went down into the [depths] of the lake,
and the place where it had gone with him was not known.
Then [the Majesty] [of the Dual] [King] Nebka, justified, had the wife of Webaoner taken to the field north of the Residence,
and he set fire to her,
[and] [she] [was] thrown into the river.
Look, [this is] a wonder that happened [in] the time of your father the Dual King Nebka, among the deeds of the chief lector priest Webaoner.
Then the Majesty of the Dual King Khufu, justified, said:

Have 1,000 loaves of bread, 100 jugs of beer, 1 ox and 2 pellets of incense presented to the Dual King Nebka, justified, and have 1 cake, 1 jug of beer, a large joint of meat and 1 pellet of incense given to the chief lector priest Webaoner.
Then Baufra stood up to speak, and he said:
Let me have Your Majesty hear of a wonder that happened in the time of your father Snefru, justified, among the deeds of the chief lector priest Djadjaemankh [...]
bright (?) [yester]day [...] fresh [in remembrance]
praised [...] the day of those [...] which had not been done (?), caused to happen.
[Now His Majesty the Dual King Snefru, justified, had gone round all the rooms] of the palace, life, prosperity, health, to seek [a refreshment (?)] for himself,
[but he did not find it.]
[Then His Majesty said:]
Go, bring me the chief lector priest and scribe of the [book], Djadjaemankh!
He was brought [to] him at once.
Then His Majesty said to him:
[I have gone round all the rooms] of the palace, [life, prosperity, health], to seek a refreshment for myself,
and I have not found it.
Then Djadjaemankh said to him:
If only Your Majesty would go to the lake of the palace, life, prosperity, health, and fit out a boat for yourself with all the beautiful women of the inner part of your palace!
Your Majesty's heart will be refreshed at seeing them row, rowing downstream and upstream.
You will see the beautiful marshes of your lake,
you will see its fields and its beautiful banks,
and your heart will be refreshed by it.
I will indeed make my rowing trip.
Have brought to me twenty oars of ebony worked with gold, their grips of *seqeb*-wood worked with electrum.

Have brought to me twenty women, the most beautiful in body, with firm breasts and braided hair, who have not been opened by childbirth; and have brought to me twenty nets, and have these nets given to these women, their clothes laid aside.
Then it was done according to all that His Majesty commanded.
And they rowed downstream and upstream,
and His Majesty's heart was happy at seeing them row.
Then one who was at the stroke caught (?) [...] in her braid,
and a fish-pendant of new turquoise fell into the water.
Then she fell silent and did not row,
and her side fell silent and did not row.
Then His Majesty said:
Are you not rowing?
Then they said:
Our stroke has fallen silent and does not row.
Then His Majesty said to her:
[Why] are you not rowing?
Then she said:
[It is] a fish-pendant [of] new [turquoise that] fell into the water.
Then he [put] her [at the stroke].
[Then His Majesty said] to her:
[I] wish (?) [to give you its like as] compensation.
Then [she said]:
I [want my] own thing [more than its like].
Then [His Majesty] said:
[Go, bring me] the [chief] lector priest [Djadjaemankh]!
[He was brought to him at once.]
Then His Majesty said:
Djadjaemankh, my brother, I have done as you said,
and His Majesty's heart was refreshed at seeing them row.
Then a fish-pendant of new turquoise belonging to one of the strokes fell into the water,
and she fell silent and did not row,
and so she upset her side.
Then I said to her:
Why are you not rowing?
Then she said to me:
It is a fish-pendant of new turquoise that fell into the water.
Then I said to her:
Row!
See, I will replace it.
Then she said to me:
I want my own thing more than its like.
Then the chief lector priest Djadjaemankh said what he said by magic.
Then he put one side of the water of the lake on top of the other, and he found the fish-pendant lying on a potsherd [...] potsherd.
Then he brought it, and it was given to its owner.
Now as for the water, it was twelve cubits [deep] in its middle,
and it came to twenty-four cubits after it was folded back.
Then he said what he said by magic,
and he brought the waters of the lake back to their position.
His Majesty spent the day in festivity with the whole palace, life, prosperity, health.
He came out and rewarded the chief lector priest Djadjaemankh with every good thing.
See, a wonder that happened in the time of your father the Dual King Snefru, justified, among the deeds of the chief lector priest and scribe of the book Djadjaemankh.
Then the Majesty of the Dual King Khufu, justified, said:

Let an offering of 1,000 loaves, 100 jugs of beer, one ox and two balls of incense be made to the Majesty of the Dual King Snefru, justified, and let one cake, one jar of beer and one ball of incense be given to the chief lector priest and scribe of the book Djadjaemankh,
for I have seen a token of his learning.
And it was done according to all that His Majesty commanded.
Then the king's son Hordjedef stood up to speak, and he said:
[It is talk] of an instance [of a wonder now past], from what those who have passed away knew;
one cannot tell truth [from] falsehood.
[There is, under] Your Majesty, in your own time, [one] who is not known,
[a knowing man who makes the ignorant know.]
Then His Majesty said:
What [is it], Hordjedef, my [son]?
[Then the king's son] Hordjedef [said]:
There is a commoner named Djedi, who lives in Djed-Snefru, justified.
He is a commoner of 110 years,
and he eats 500 loaves, a shoulder of beef as meat, and drinks 100 jugs of beer, to this very day.
He knows how to join a severed head;
he knows how to make a lion walk behind him, its leash on the ground;
he knows the number of the *ipwt* [chambers] of the sanctuary of Thoth.
Now the Majesty of the Dual King Khufu, justified, had been spending his days seeking for himself the *ipwt* of the sanctuary of Thoth, to make their like for himself for his horizon.
Then His Majesty said:
You yourself, Hordjedef my son, shall bring him to me.
Then ships were made ready for the king's son Hordjedef.
He travelled upstream to Djed-Snefru, justified.
After the ships had moored at the riverbank, he travelled by land, seated in a carrying-chair of ebony, its poles of *sesnedjem*-wood, overlaid with gold.
When he reached Djedi, the carrying-chair was set down.
He stood up to greet him, and found him lying on a mat at the threshold (?) of his [house],
a servant at his head rubbing him,
another rubbing his feet.
Then the king's son Hordjedef said:

Your condition is like that of one who lives before growing old, in spite of old age, the time of mooring, the time of burial, the time of joining the earth: sleeping until daylight, free of illness, without a wheezing cough (?).
Such is the greeting for a revered man.
I have come here to summon you on an errand of my father Khufu, justified, so that you may eat the fine things the king gives, the provisions of those who are in his following,
and that he may convey you through a good lifetime to your fathers who are in the necropolis.
Then this Djedi said:
In peace, in peace, Hordjedef, king's son, [beloved] of his father!
May your father Khufu, justified, favour you;
may he advance your place among the elders;
may your *ka* [vital force] contend in [every] matter against the adversary;
may your *ba* [soul] know the hidden (?) ways to the portal of Him Who Clothes the Weary One.
Such is the greeting for a king's son.
Then the king's son Hordjedef stretched out his arms to him
and raised him up.
He went with him to the riverbank, giving him his arm.
Then Djedi said:
Let me be given one of the barges,
so that it may bring me my children and my writings.
Then two barges were made ready for him, with their crews.
Djedi came downstream in the broad ship in which the king's son Hordjedef was.
When he reached the Residence, the king's son Hordjedef went in to report to the Majesty of the Dual King Khufu, justified.
Then the king's son Hordjedef said:
O Sovereign, life, prosperity, health, my lord, I have brought Djedi.
Then His Majesty said:
Go, bring him to me!
His Majesty went to the columned hall of the palace, life, prosperity, health,
and Djedi was ushered in to him.
Then His Majesty said:
How is it, Djedi, that I have not been allowed to see you?
Then Djedi said:
It is the one who is summoned who comes, O Sovereign, life, prosperity, health.
Summon me, and see, I have come.
Then His Majesty said:
Is it true, what is said, that you know how to join a severed head?
Then Djedi said:
Yes, I do know [how], O Sovereign, life, prosperity, health, my lord.
Then His Majesty said:
Have brought to me a prisoner who is in the prison, whose punishment has been decreed.
Then Djedi said:
But not on people, O Sovereign, life, prosperity, health, my lord!
See, it is not commanded that such a thing be done to the noble flock.
Then a goose was brought to him, its head cut off.
Then the goose was put on the west side of the columned hall, and its head on the east side of the columned hall.
Then Djedi said his sayings of magic.
And the goose stood up, waddling, and its head likewise.
When the one had reached the other, the goose stood cackling.
Then he had a *khetaa*-bird brought to him,
and the same was done to it.
Then His Majesty had an ox brought to him, its head felled to the ground.
Then Djedi said what he said by magic,
and the ox stood up behind him, its tether fallen to the ground.
Then King Khufu, justified, said:
And what of the saying that you know the number of the *ipwt* of the sanctuary of [Thoth]?
Then Djedi said:
If you please, I do not know their number, O Sovereign, life, prosperity, health, my lord,
but I do know the place where it is.
Then His Majesty said:
Where is it, then?
Then this Djedi said:
There is a chest of flint there, in a room named 'Inventory', in Heliopolis.
[See, it is] in that chest.
Then Djedi said:
O Sovereign, life, prosperity, health, my lord, see, it is not I who will bring it to you.
Then His Majesty said:
Who, then, will bring it to me?
Then Djedi said:
It is the eldest of the three children who are in the womb of Ruddjedet who will bring it to you.
Then His Majesty said:
I do want it, this that you will tell [me]:
who is she, this Ruddjedet?
Then Djedi said:
She is the wife of a *wab* [pure] priest of Ra, lord of Sakhebu, who is pregnant with three children of Ra, lord of Sakhebu.
He has said of her
that they will exercise this excellent office in this entire land,
and the eldest of them will be Greatest of Seers in Heliopolis.
Then His Majesty's heart fell into sadness at this.
Then Djedi said:
What is this mood, O Sovereign, life, prosperity, health, my lord?
Is it because of the three children I have spoken of?
Then your son, then his son, then one of them.
Then His Majesty said:
When will she give birth, then, Ruddjedet?
[Then Djedi said:]
She will give birth in the first month of *Peret* [Emergence], on day 15.
Then His Majesty said:
But (?) the sandbanks of the Two Fishes (?) will be cut off.
I would myself labour (?) for it; then I would see the temple of Ra, lord of Sakhebu.
Then Djedi said:
Then I will make there be four cubits of water on the sandbanks of the Two Fishes (?).
His Majesty went to his palace.
Then His Majesty said:
Let Djedi be assigned to the house of the king's son Hordjedef, to live with him.
Make his rations 1,000 loaves, 100 jugs of beer, one ox and 100 bunches of leeks.
And it was done according to all that His Majesty commanded.
One of those days it happened that Ruddjedet was in labour pains,
and her giving birth was difficult.
Then the Majesty of Ra, lord of Sakhebu, said to Isis, Nephthys, Meskhenet, Heqet and Khnum:

Please go and deliver Ruddjedet of the three children who are in her womb, who will exercise this excellent office in this entire land. They will build your temples, they will provision your altars, they will make your offering tables flourish, they will increase your divine offerings.
These gods set out, having taken their forms [...] as musicians,
Khnum with them carrying the baggage.
They arrived at the house of Rawoser
and found him standing with his kilt upside down.
And they held out to him their *menat*-necklaces and sistra.
Then he said to them:
My ladies, see, it is a woman who is in pain,
and her giving birth is difficult.
Then they said:
Let us see her;
see, we know how to deliver.
Then he said to them:
Go in!
They went in before Ruddjedet.
Then they shut the room upon her and themselves [...] her [upper house] (?) with her.
Then Isis placed herself in front of her, Nephthys behind her, and Heqet hastened the birth.
Then Isis said:
Do not be strong in her womb, in this your name of Userref.
Then this child slid out onto her hands, a child of one cubit,
his bones firm,
the covering (?) of his limbs of gold,
his headcloth of true lapis lazuli.
They washed him, his navel cord was cut, and he was laid on a cloth upon a brick.
Then Meskhenet presented herself to him
and said:
A king who will exercise kingship in this entire land!
Khnum gave health to his body.
Then Isis placed herself in front of her, Nephthys behind her, and Heqet hastened the birth.
Then Isis said:
Do not kick in her womb, in this your name of Sahra.
Then this child slid out onto her hands, a child of one cubit,
his bones firm,
the covering (?) of his limbs [of gold],
his headcloth of true lapis lazuli.
They washed him, his navel cord was cut, and he was laid on a cloth upon a brick.
Then Meskhenet presented herself to him
and said:
A king who will exercise kingship in this entire land!
And Khnum gave health to his limbs.
Then Isis placed herself in front of her, Nephthys behind her, and Heqet hastened the birth.
Then Isis said:
Do not be dark in her womb, in this your name of Keku.
Then this child slid out onto her hands, a child of one cubit,
his bones firm,
the covering (?) of his limbs of gold,
his headcloth of true lapis lazuli.
Then Meskhenet presented herself to him
and said:
A king who will exercise kingship in this entire land!
And Khnum gave health to his limbs.
They washed him, his navel cord was cut, and he was laid on a cloth upon a brick.
These gods came out, having delivered Ruddjedet of the three children.
Then they said:
Let your heart be glad, Rawoser!
See, three children have been born to you.
Then he said to them:
My ladies, what can I do for you?
Please give this barley to your porter,
and take it for yourselves as payment for *tenemu*-beer (?) [...] for (?) *nemu* (?).
Then Khnum loaded himself with the barley.
They set off for the place they had come from.
Then Isis said to these gods:
What is this, that we have come here without working a wonder for these children, which we might report to their father who sent us?
Then they fashioned three crowns of the lord, may he live, prosper and be healthy,
and they put them in the barley.
Then they made the sky turn to storm and rain,
and they turned back to the house.
Then they said:
Please put the barley here in a sealed room until we come back from making music in the north.
Then they put the [barley] in a sealed room.
Then Ruddjedet purified herself with a purification of fourteen days.
Then she said to her maidservant:
Is the house provided for?
And she said:
It is provided with every good thing except jars: they have not been brought.
Then Ruddjedet said:
Why, then, have jars not been brought?
Then the maidservant said:
There is nothing here to make use of except the barley of these musicians,
and it is in a room under their seal.
Then Ruddjedet said:
Go down and bring some of it.
Rawoser will give them its replacement when he comes back.
The maidservant went and opened the room,
and she heard the sound of singing, music, dancing and jubilation, everything that is done for a king, in the room.
She went
and repeated all she had heard to Ruddjedet.
And she went round the room,
but she did not find the place where it was being done.
Then she put her temple to the sack and found that it was being done inside it.
Then she put [it] in a chest, which was put inside another, sealed and bound with leather.
She put it in a room that held her belongings, and sealed it.
Rawoser came, returning from the fields,
and Ruddjedet repeated this matter to him,
and his heart was happier than anything.
They sat down to a day of festivity.
Some days after this, Ruddjedet quarrelled with the maidservant over something and had her punished with a beating.
Then the maidservant said to the people who were in the house:
Is she to do this, this (?) [to me]?
She has borne three kings!
I will go [and] tell it to the Majesty of the Dual King Khufu, justified!
She went and found her eldest brother by her mother tying flax yarn on the threshing floor.
Then he said to her:
Where are you off to, little girl?
And she repeated this matter to him.
Then her brother said to her:
Is this really what you should do, coming to me so that I join in a denunciation?
Then he took a length (?) of flax to her
and gave her a bad beating.
The maidservant went to fetch herself a scoop of water,
and a crocodile took her.
Her brother went [to] tell it to Ruddjedet.
He found Ruddjedet sitting with her head on her knees, her heart sadder than anything.
Then he said to her:
My lady, why are you in this mood?
Then she said:
It is that little one who grew up in the house!
See, she has gone off, saying:
'I will go and denounce [her]!'
Then he hung his head
and said:
My lady, she came to tell me [...] my (?) [...], so that she might do [it] with me beside her (?),
and I gave her a bad beating.
Then [she] went to [draw] a little water for herself,
and a crocodile took her [...]
